Historyof Organization
Youth Alternatives is a department of the City of Cheyenne and is a govermment agency. The
program was established in 1971 to provide services to youth placed on probation in the City of
Cheyenne.The program received national recognition as an exemplary Model Cities Project.
Congressman Teno Roncalio spoke about the program before Congress in1974 and in1975 the
program was selected to appear in a book of exemplary projects.
In 1977, the program received a letter of commendation from President Jimmy Carter and the
George Washington Honor Medal from the Freedom Foundation in Philadelphia. In 1980, the
distinguished Jefferson Award, from the Jefferson Foundations was awarded to the program.
In 1990, the program was recognized for outstanding volunteer achievement by President George
Bush and was designated as the 247lh Point of Light and in 1991 the program received a medal
commemorating this honor at a ceremony in Florida.
To date, our services have grown toinclude: family counseling, court services, pre-court diversion,
probation, juvenile alcohol&drug intervention program, electronic monitoring, work al term at ives
program, group services, schools er vic s, family crisis nter vent ion, community challenge course,
and Special Friends - our mentoring program.
Youth Alternatives provides the City of Cheyenne with a coordinated response to the needs of
troubled youth in the community.The program utilizes the community as a tool to modify the
inappropriate behavior of troubled youth.The program is designed to intervene in the lives of
into the juvenile justice system.The program attempts to assist troubled youth to see themselves
as better people and the world as less hostile by providing preventative, supportive, and
rehab il it at ive services.

A.Population
This proposal will concentrate on families with children 5 to 18 years of age, who have been
identified as having at least one or more risk factors in their lives (i.e. poverty, abuse, neglect,
domestic violence family conflict, substance abuse, school difficulties, delinquency, etc.),
including:
1.families with identified risk factors in their lives who are not involved in the child
protection and/or juvenile justice system.
2.families who are currently being served by the child protection and/or juvenile justice
system (i.e. children returning home from placement, on probation, in foster care, etc.).
3.under-served families (i.e. focusing on Hispanic and African-American families) who
traditionally do not voluntarily access services but maybe more vulnerable to out of home
placement because of multiple risk factors in their lives.
B.Intent of Program
The intent of this proposal is to two-fold.
1.To strengthen the ability of parents to provide supportive care for their children. The
resulting outcome should be the prevention and/or reduction of the number of youth
entering or penetrating further into the juvenile justice and/or child protection system.
2.To provide in-home support services to under-served families in Laramie County.
C.Geographic Area to Be Covered
The geographic area will be the City of Cheyenne and the surrounding areas of
Laramie County.

Letter of Support: Youth Alternatives Proposal
I am writing in support of the proposal submitted by the Office of Youth Alternatives (YA). We have
partnered with YA for over 25 years to provide both in-school and after-school support to the
success by addressing their emotional, behavioral and family needs.
In addition we have partnered on a significant number of other efforts that have benefitted our
students, parents and the community. Some of those eforts include; the development of the
Adolescent Day Treatment Center for students with emotional and behavioral problems; the
Educational Annex, formerly callthe PEP Center, for students who are expelled or suspended from,
school and a variety of other programs designed to keep our kids in school.
As the Director of Special Services for Laramie County School District 1, I know the value of the
services provided by YA. Many of the Districts children live in low-income, single-parent
households, which may cause the families to be overwhelmed and stressed.As a result, these
children may be at risk for poor school attendance, poor school performance, poorchoices and poor
behavior, resulting in increased drop-out rates, delinquent behaviors and eventual placement
outside the home.
The School District regularly partners with Youth Alternatives/Special Friends to improve the well-
being of the children and families in our District.Specifically:
1.Refer students and parents needing mentoring and parenting support.
2.Assist with student assessments and program evaluations.
3.Allow the program to utilize school facilities to run its after-school programs.
4.Assist with transportation after school and during the summer.
The School District and Youth Alternatives have worked closely together for many years and look
forward to our mutual efforts in meeting the needs of families in our community.
Sincerely,
Alice Hunter
Director of Special Services

2.Cost Benefits:
The 2008 independent longitudinal recidivism study reviewed 1,153 participants in Youth
Alternatives court service programs.The study indicated 87.2 % of the youth did not re-offend at
the District Court level.The only court that can remove youth from their home is the District
Court.Average yearly cost for out-of-home placement is estimated to be from $30,000 to
$45,000.Therefore, the 1,005.4 youth who did not end up in out-of-home placement because of
prevention services at Youth Alternatives saved the State approximately $3,016,200 at a
minimum.The 2012 review of previously mentored youth over the age of 18 indicated the
81.2%were successful, further supporting the cost benefits of our early intervention programs.

County. The program also has contracts with a variety of sources like Laramie County Juvenile
